inputs.share_count_basis: 402.337M shares outstanding on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (26 Oct 2026) + 0.3M dilutive options/RSUs (Q3 EPS table) + 1.7M unvested performance RSAs/RSUs excluded from diluted EPS. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. A further 6.2M anti-dilutive options/awards are out of the money at the current price and are not counted.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back (194) - 9M-2025 (153) + 9M-2026 (112) = 153, which matches the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation line; CoStar publishes no combined figure including withholding taxes, so 'Repurchase of restricted stock to satisfy tax withholding obligations' is added: 75 - 64 + 24 = 35. FY2025's 194 (and Q3-2025's 71) is NOT a baseline: the Q3-2026 10-Q attributes the year-on-year fall to 'accelerated stock-based compensation recognized for certain Matterport employees in the prior-year period'. 2026 run-rate is 41/38/32 per quarter.
inputs.fy0: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 (FY2025 + 9M-2026 - 9M-2025); Y1 = twelve months to Sep 2027
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows: ~4.5% 10-year Treasury + ~5% ERP x beta ~1.0 = ~9.5% cost of equity; debt is a single $1.0bn 2.8% note against a ~$12.5bn market cap, so WACC is rounded to 9.5%. The same rate is used in every scenario -- risk is charged through the scenario weights, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is inside EBITDA already; lease liabilities are not added to net debt. No separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest of $17M (Domain agent-ownership models; $26M bought in during 2026) deducted at book in the equity bridge; flows are not otherwise reduced.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company: tech, SaaS, consumer internet, marketplaces'). CoStar is a subscription real-estate information and marketplace business (89% subscription revenue); FCF, EBITDA and net debt all mean what the engine assumes. Fresh build, no prior DCF and no MEMORY entry. No Analysis JSON existed at build time -- scenario axes are drawn from the 10-K/10-Q MD&A and the kpis table. FY0 is the TTM to Sep-2026 rather than FY2025 because three quarters of FY2026 are already in the 30 Sep balance sheet (cash fell 1,633 -> 500 on $668M buybacks and $789M of acquisitions, chiefly Zonda at $815M closed 21 Aug 2026); starting the flows from FY2025 would count that cash twice. INTEREST: the company is now in net DEBT ($1.0bn notes vs $500M cash), TTM net interest income is ~$20M and Q3-2026 was a net expense, so nothing is stripped; the forward build is unlevered from EBITDA. REPORTED FCF: TTM OCF 617 less TTM capex 260 (campus + other lines both) = 357, and is after a one-off $99M Brown Judgment payment (Matterport litigation, funded from restricted cash). DATA FLAG: Metrics.csv CapEx for FY2025 and the 2025-26 quarters carries only the 'new campuses' line (FY2025 307) and omits 'Purchases of property, equipment, and other assets' (82), so CSV FreeCashFlow for FY2025 (123) is overstated by 82; true FY2025 FCF is 41. Not corrected here -- needs `make fix`. BUYBACKS: funded -- $500M ASR plus $168M 10b5-1 in 9M-2026 (16.5M shares at ~$40), $832M authorisation remaining; the flat share count is being paid for in cash, although at prices well above today's. ADJUSTED EBITDA excludes acquisition/integration costs ($27M 9M-2026, $56M 9M-2025), which recur for a serial acquirer; the margin paths are shaded for this rather than carrying a separate line. D&A in the engine is depreciation and software amortisation only (~3% of revenue); acquired-intangible amortisation (~$270M/yr) is left out so no tax shield is credited on largely non-deductible stock-deal intangibles.

equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet, equity attributable to NCI

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (9.3%) is 35% below revenue 5yr CAGR (14.4%); EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful (EPS 0.93 -> 0.02 FY2022-FY2025; owner FCF went from roughly +310 in FY2022 to about -340 in FY2025 on Homes.com marketing, campus capex and Matterport award acceleration). Neither historical rate is used for the forward path: reported growth has been acquisition-fed (Matterport, Domain, Zonda) and pro-forma growth in Q3-2026 was 6.1%.
historical_growth.notes: FY2022-FY2025 and FY2020-FY2025, annual rows. Owner FCF = OCF - both capex lines - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes - interest income. Reported FCF fell far less than owner FCF because $214M/$213M/$110M of interest income on the pre-acquisition cash pile sat inside OCF in FY2023-25 and SBC plus withholding taxes rose from 98 to 269; the reported series materially overstated what the operations produced.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 9.0% is mostly arithmetic: pro-forma Q3-2026 revenue of 975 (Zonda in for the full quarter) annualises to ~3,900 against a 3,674 TTM base, plus ~1.25%/quarter sequential growth. Organic growth after that is 5.5-6%, in line with Q3-2026 pro-forma growth of 6.1% and TTM net new bookings of $248M (~7.5% of subscription revenue) but above the Q3 bookings run-rate ($37M x 4 = ~4.5%).
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.7% TTM, 17.3% in H1-2026 and 24.1% in Q3-2026 (Commercial 36.6%, Residential 10.7% after marketing was cut from 200 to 171). Y1 at 23% sits just under the Q3 exit rate to allow for the seasonally heavier H1 marketing; the path reaches 34% by year 9, slightly above the 31-33% CoStar earned in FY2021-22 before the Homes.com investment.
base.capex_note: Y1 4.5% absorbs $75M of accrued, unpaid campus capex (Richmond was placed in service in Q2-2026); ordinary capex has run 2.2-2.5% of revenue and 3.0% is used once owned campuses need maintaining.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Cash taxes were a $3M net refund in 9M-2026 and $73M in FY2025; ramped to 24% (21% federal plus state, Australia and UK) by year 3 rather than carrying the shelter forward.

scenario_narratives.base: The commercial franchise (CoStar, LoopNet, about half of revenue at a ~36% segment margin) keeps growing high-single digits on price and international launches, but the bookings slowdown is real: the renewal rate has slipped from 92% (FY2021) to 88%, cancellations have risen from 8% to 12%, and Q3-2026 net new bookings were $37M against $84M a year earlier, which management blames on economic headwinds, a sales force that grew slower than planned, and competition. Organic growth therefore settles at 5.5-6% rather than the low-teens the reported history shows (that history is Matterport, Domain and Zonda). Residential stops being a drain as Homes.com marketing is cut -- segment Adjusted EBITDA already moved from -$69M to +$49M year on year in Q3 -- and consolidated margin climbs back to 34% over nine years, roughly where the company was before Homes.com. SBC runs about 4.5% of revenue including withholding taxes, drifting to 4%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q3 bookings dip proves cyclical: rates ease, apartment and residential transaction volumes recover, the sales force is rebuilt and net new bookings return above $300M a year. Homes.com agent memberships reach scale now that marketing has been reset, Apartments.com holds share against Zillow Rentals, and Matterport plus the AI search products lift pricing across CoStar and LoopNet. Growth runs 9-10% for five years and, with residential earning portal-like margins, consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 39% -- still well below REA or Rightmove, because CoStar keeps a large research headcount.
scenario_narratives.bear: The deterioration in renewals is structural rather than cyclical: brokers and owners consolidate and trim seats, Zillow and others take multifamily advertising share from Apartments.com, and Homes.com never earns a return on the several billion dollars spent, so marketing has to stay high just to hold traffic. Net new bookings stay near the Q3-2026 run-rate, organic growth falls to ~3%, and margin stalls at 26% as the commercial segment absorbs wage inflation and the residential segment hovers around break-even. Acquisitions continue to be paid for in cash at prices that do not earn their cost of capital. Terminal multiple capped at 15x for a business that has stopped compounding.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: its premise is simply that the latest trend continues -- renewal rate down four points in five years and Q3 net new bookings down 56% -- and it needs nothing new to go wrong; there is no balance-sheet or going-concern risk, which is why it is not higher. Base held at 50%: it assumes the commercial franchise is intact and residential losses are over, both of which Q3-2026 segment results support. Bull cut to 25%: it needs three independent things at once -- a real-estate cycle recovery, a bookings recovery, and Homes.com monetisation that has not yet been shown.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CoStar is valued on what the operations leave for owners after stock compensation, not on Adjusted EBITDA. On that basis the last twelve months produced about $170M ($270M before a one-off litigation payment) on $3.7bn of revenue, so almost all of the value rests on margins recovering from ~20% toward the mid-30s as Homes.com spending is cut and campus construction ends. The Q3-2026 quarter supports the direction; the fall in net new bookings and the renewal rate caps how much growth can be assumed alongside it. Cash that funded the valuation in prior years has been spent: the company moved from $4.7bn of cash at the end of 2024 to $0.5bn of net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-heavy: the base case depends on a 34% Adjusted EBITDA margin that the company last earned in FY2021-22; each point of terminal-year margin is worth roughly $0.75 a share, more if the whole path shifts.

Net new bookings ($37M in Q3-2026 vs $84M) and the renewal rate (88%) are leading indicators; if Q4-2026 and Q1-2027 bookings stay near $40M the base growth path is too high and the bear path becomes the central case.

Capital allocation: $3.1bn spent on acquisitions and $1.2bn on buybacks at ~$40-70 a share in under two years; the model gives no credit or penalty for future deals, and Adjusted EBITDA excludes their integration costs.
Homes.com: residential segment margin has turned positive only because marketing was cut; whether traffic and agent memberships hold at the lower spend is not yet visible.
No Q4 or FY2027 guidance was available in the filings on hand (10-Qs carry only directional segment commentary); year-1 revenue is built from the pro-forma Q3 run-rate.
Litigation: further Matterport shareholder suits follow the Brown Judgment, and the STR hotel antitrust class action is unresolved; nothing is provided for either.
